By Lemma <REF_0001> the functor is faithful.
Let <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> be <ACCENT_0001>tale morphisms
and let <MATH_0003> be a
morphism compatible with canonical descent data.
We will prove that <MATH_0004> is the base change of a morphism <MATH_0005>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Let <MATH_0006> be an open subscheme. Consider
<MATH_0007>. This is an open subscheme
of <MATH_0008> which is compatible with the canonical
descent datum on <MATH_0009>. This means that the
two inverse images of <MATH_0010> by the projections
<MATH_0011> agree. Since <MATH_0012>
is surjective (as the base change of <MATH_0013>) we conclude
that <MATH_0014> is the inverse image of some subset <MATH_0015>.
Since <MATH_0016> is open, our assumption on <MATH_0017> implies that <MATH_0018>
is open.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Let <MATH_0019> be an affine open covering.
By the result of the preceding paragraph we obtain an open
covering <MATH_0020> such that
<MATH_0021>.
If we can prove there exists a morphism <MATH_0022>
whose base change is the morphism
<MATH_0023>
then we can glue these morphisms to a morphism <MATH_0024>
(using faithfulness). In this way we reduce to the case that
<MATH_0025> is affine. In particular <MATH_0026> is separated
(Schemes, Lemma <REF_0002>).

<STRUCT_0005><STRUCT_0006>
Assume <MATH_0027> is separated. Then the graph <MATH_0028> of <MATH_0029>
is a closed subscheme of
<MATH_0030>
by Schemes, Lemma <REF_0003>.
On the other hand the graph is open for example
because it is a section of an <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism
(Proposition <REF_0004>).
Since <MATH_0031> is a morphism of descent data, the two inverse images of
<MATH_0032> under the projections
<MATH_0033> are the same.
Hence arguing as in the second paragraph of the proof we
find an open and closed subscheme <MATH_0034>
whose base change to <MATH_0035> gives <MATH_0036>. Then
<MATH_0037> is an <ACCENT_0003>tale morphism whose base change
to <MATH_0038> is an isomorphism. This means that <MATH_0039>
is universally bijective, hence an isomorphism
by Theorem <REF_0005>.
Thus <MATH_0040> is the graph of a morphism <MATH_0041>
and the base change of this morphism is <MATH_0042> as desired.
